Pre-Gestational Diabetes
• Pre-existing DM
• Type 1 usually
• Increased incidence of type 2
Gestational Diabetes
• Occurs with pregnancy
• Diagnosed usually after 24 weeks
• Increased risk for DM 2 later in life
Two Types
22

2
Systemic disorder of CHO, fat & protein metabolism
Insulin transports glucose into cells to use for energy
Without insulin- glucose cannot enter cells
Body must burn fat for energy:
Ketone bodies are the byproduct of fat metabolism
• Accumulation of ketones can lead to ketoacidosis, coma, and death

Over 30
Obesity

Gestational Diabetes

th

1 hour later :  Blood glucose of 130-140
• slight variation on diagnosis values  w postprandial 
levels
Elevated result = more screening
Step 1: Glucose Screening 
glucose tolerance test

 3 hour OGTT 
 High carb diet (150g carbs) x 3 days before test
 Fasts- NPO except water after midnight.
 100g oral solution in morning
 Blood draws x4
Fasting=95mg/dl
1 hour =180mg/dl
2 hour =155mg/dl
3 hour =140mg/dl
Two out of three abnormal results = GDM

 GDM-A2- needs insulin

Treatment Options for GDM

13
 45-50% Complex Carbs
 20% protein
 30% fat
 1800-2200 Cal per day divided among 3 meals + 3 
snacks
increase calories by about 300kcal day
30kcal/kg of ideal body weight
 Exercise as appropriate for pregnancy

Pre-Gestational DM

15
• variable: observe for hypoglycemia
• increased requirement between 28-32 weeks
• decrease in requirement after 35 weeks
• re-assess after delivery
Insulin Requirments
• ketoacidosis is associated with fetal death
• greatest risk is near term
Goal:  Euglycemia
Management of Pre-Gestational DM

19
Blood glucose levels must be checked and 
insulin adjusted
Have dextrose 50% available
No contraindications to breastfeeding
